questions.question:
Identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error.

Jaya asked Sushmita to reminds her about the meeting.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1.**

The error lies in the 2nd part of the sentence.

As per the Subject-Verb agreement rule, The verb must agree with its Subject in Number and person. Sushmita being the 2nd person must agree with 2nd person singular verb.

Thus, **'Reminds'** should be replaced with **'remind'.**

__The infinitive is the base of the of a verb which is often preceded by 'to'.__

Thus the correct sentence will be: *Jaya asked Sushmita to remind her about the meeting.*

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement.**

Rashmi is not only smart __but very beautiful.__
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**but also very beautiful**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The conjunction pair is not only...but also__.
 
• Correlative conjunctions always come in pairs and they relate one part of the sentence to the other. "Not only... but also" can be used to connect either nouns or clauses. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Using *not only . . . but also***** in a sentence**, **parallelism**** should be the goal**. It means that the words following both parts of this correlative conjunction (i.e., *not only* and *but also*) should belong to the same parts of speech. For example, if a verb follows *not only*, then a verb should also follow *but also*. Using different parts of speech after each part of *not only . . . but also* makes the sentence imbalanced and, frankly, just awkward. 

 **Example: **He’s not only intelligent but also has a great sense of humor.

 He’s not only intelligent but also funny.

 

**Thus the correct sentence will be:** *Rashmi is not only smart but also very beautiful.*

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement.

I'll be at the parlour __near 5 P.M.__
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**till'.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• The preposition '**near'** means '**not far away in distance**'. 

 
 
• **Example**: My mother loves to sit **near **the lamp.
 
 
 
• **'Along'** is a preposition used to denote **position on a line**.
 
 
• **Example**: There was a thick line of trees **along** the road. 
 
 
 
• **'Unless'** is a conjunction which means '**except if**'
 
 
• **Example**: They won't come unless you invite them. 
 
 
 
• **'Till'** is a preposition that means **'up to the time of'**.
 
 
• **Example**: He waited** till **3 O'clock. 
 
 
 
• **'Unless'** is action-oriented conjunction hence, can't be used with time. 
 
• The usage of the other options thus makes the sentence grammatically incorrect.

 

**The correct sentence is:** I'll be at the parlour till 5 P.M.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/efb90c3647c276e117dc17fb6439410dad00fafe8f511a89c38f32cba7de65df.png] 

 
• In the given sentence,** 5 P.M.** signifies that a **preposition of time** should be used. This will help us to eliminate the two options- '**along'** and** 'near'** as they are prepositions of place.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Preposition of time**: at, since, ago, during, till, until, before, after.
 
• 
 **Preposition of direction**: above, across, along, below, behind, over.
 
 
• **Preposition of place**: In, at upon, beside, under, from, on.

questions.question:
Identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error.

If I had known about him before I will have recommended him.
questions.solution:
The erroneous part is **‘I will have**.'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The sentence starts with **‘If’. **‘If’ denotes that the question is a **conditional sentence** and more accurately, it is an example of** third conditional sentence**.
 
• Third conditional sentence is used to explain that present situation would be different if something different had happened in the past.
 
• The incident that happens first or was supposed to happen first takes a past perfect tense **(had + V3 form of verb)** in the ‘If’ clause when **‘would/should/could have’ **is present in the main clause that expresses the hypothetical situation that could have happened.
 
• In the question, ‘If I had known about him before’ is the incident that is supposed to happen first. Therefore, ‘would have recommended’ (had + V3 form of verb) should be the correct verb form used here.

Therefore, the corrected sentence is: "*If I had known about him before, I **would have **recommended him."*
